Optional YouTube Shorts control chosen in FocusBuddy settings

FocusBuddy can inspect YouTube view structure. If you also turn on Block YouTube Shorts in FocusBuddy, it attempts one Back action when the observed Shorts player appears. You can turn either setting off at any time.

This optional Android service can inspect YouTube’s on-screen structure while you use YouTube. Android grants accessibility access only after you turn the service on in system settings. You can turn it off there at any time.

In debug builds, FocusBuddy records limited YouTube event types, view classes, view IDs, and the reel UI signal in device logs. It does not read or log screen text, video titles, or descriptions. FocusBuddy does not send these logs online.
Detection uses a view ID observed on one phone and YouTube version. Other versions may miss Shorts or cause an unwanted Back action. You can turn blocking off above.
When this is on and the Shorts player is recognized, FocusBuddy tries one Back action. Regular YouTube videos stay available. You can turn this off whenever you like.
